lyrics:
[Intro: strummed acoustic guitar, a sigh, crickets]

[Verse 1: raspy male voice, quiet]
Towels on the railing, fire's burning low
The kids are getting quiet, 'cause they know
The cooler's by the door, the bags are by the stair
You're looking at the water like it's already not there

[Chorus: second voice in harmony, band enters softly]
Every summer has a Sunday night
Every party has a kitchen light
Every kid has got a driveway and a wave goodbye
Every summer has a Sunday night

[Verse 2: voice warmer, bass and brushes]
I used to fight it, used to sulk the whole way home
Used to waste the last day wishing it would slow
My father did the same, he'd go quiet by noon
Took me forty years to hear a different tune

[Chorus: fuller, electric guitar answering]
Every summer has a Sunday night
Every party has a kitchen light
Every kid has got a driveway and a wave goodbye
Every summer has a Sunday night

[Guitar Solo: slow, bluesy, electric]

[Bridge: acoustic and voice, almost spoken]
That's not the sad part. That's the frame.
You don't hang a picture without one.

[Verse 3: quiet, to her]
So come sit down. There's an hour left of gold.
I'm not gonna spend it getting old.

[Final Chorus: full band, crowd of family voices]
Every summer has a Sunday night
Every party has a kitchen light
Every kid has got a driveway and a wave goodbye
Every summer has a Sunday night
And tonight's a good one

[Outro: acoustic guitar, a screen door, a loon on the lake]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 70 BPM, 4/4, G major. A slow, easy acoustic ballad with a country ache.

VOICE: Male, raspy and a little nasal, a rock singer singing quietly. A second voice joins in close harmony on the choruses, and a family of voices sings the last one. The bridge is nearly spoken.

INSTRUMENTS: Strummed acoustic guitar throughout, a second acoustic guitar picking, bass, a drum kit with brushes then light sticks, an electric guitar with a clean, bluesy, sustained tone for the solo, a little pedal steel, crickets and lake sounds.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, acoustic guitar. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:46 Chorus 1. 1:12 Verse 2. 1:44 Chorus 2. 2:10 Guitar solo. 2:36 Bridge. 2:52 Verse 3. 3:08 Final chorus. 3:40 Outro, a screen door and a loon, ends 3:58.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1980s acoustic rock ballad: warm, dry and simple, guitars and voice close, band gentle behind.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'That's not the sad part. That's the frame.' at 2:36.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original uses its proverb to explain a heartbreak. An older man uses the same shape of saying to make peace with endings in general, and to enjoy the last hour.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Wistful, remembering, accepting, present.
